title: Flunking a year of high school; the Glee Club and Professor Jackson
summary: He stayed back a year over a missing notebook and sang in the Glee Club under A. S. Jackson, who made students sing notes before they could play.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah. Well, let's see, what about Lloyd Hunter's band? That was --
Well, I joined Lloyd's band in 1935.
Oh, well, that's too far ahead. Let's not jump that far. Well, let's see, now, in '30, you were still in high school.
I was still in high school.
Now, you told me about graduating from high school. You said you got flunked one year.
I had to stay in one year because I didn't have a notebook. As I said, it was three of us that had to stay in my class. It was Ruth Love and John Collins.
Neither of them played instruments, did they?
No, but they were in the Glee Club, see. We were singing in the Glee Club.
Oh, yeah, you didn't tell me about the Glee Club. You joined --
Well, I was in singing and all like that.
Was it a good choir master?
Oh, yes, very much so. Professor Jackson, A. S. Jackson, Jr.
Oh, I see.
He was a very, very good teacher.
Well, did you get an opportunity to read some music, then?
Oh, yes. Well, truthfully, he was one of these kind of teachers that, if you couldn't sing your notes, you couldn't play your instrument, see.
Oh. You had to know your music first.
You had to know the music first.
Oh, very good. Well, did you learn solfeggio P any (unintelligible)?
And he would have you stand up at the blackboard with your back to him. And he would hit a note and you would have to tell him what that note was.
But all the people couldn't do that, could they?
You learned in his class. I could tell you any note you hit.
Can you now?
Almost.
Is that right?
I used -- you know, perfect pitch.
